params.method: MEASURED from assembly_valheim.dll 1.0.12. WearNTear::UpdateSupport: support(child) = max over touching neighbours of support(n)*(1 - loss*(d+0.1)), d being centre-of-mass distance, loss the child's horizontalLoss or a Lerp to verticalLoss by the support direction's angle; a piece whose collider overlaps the `terrain` layer is pinned to maxSupport. WearNTear::HaveSupport: alive iff support >= minSupport. WearNTear::GetMaterialProperties gives the table as a pure function of m_materialType. The reason this had to run offline: UpdateWear begins `if (ZNetScene.OutsideActiveArea(pos)) { m_support = GetMaxSupport(); return; }`, so support is only ever EVALUATED when a player is nearby and an unsound bridge looks perfect in a save until the operator walks onto it.

params.method: MEASURED for persistence, INFERRED for drift. Persistence is a complete chain: all five ship prefabs carry ZNetView.m_persistent = 1 and m_type = 1 (ZDO.ObjectType.Prioritized) (scanned off the loaded prefabs); ZNetView.Awake copies that into the ZDO's DataFlags bit 4, which is what ZDO.get_Persistent reads; and the save clone builder ZDOMan::PrepareSave -> GetSaveClonePerChunk -> AddObjectsPerChunk keeps a ZDO iff `zdo.Persistent` and its prefab is not in Game.PortalPrefabHash. So a spawned Longship is written to the chunked save. DRIFT IS NOT MEASURED AND CANNOT BE FROM THIS HOST: Valheim has no mooring mechanic, and Ship::CustomFixedUpdate returns unless IsOwner, forces m_speed=Stop and m_rudderValue=0 when m_players.Count == 0, and then still applies buoyancy/damping AddForceAtPosition plus ApplyEdgeForce every tick -- so an unmanned boat is inert while nobody is in its active area and subject to wave forces while somebody is. THE OPERATOR IS THE FIRST REAL TEST. If a boat is found far from its berth, the cause is here and not in the terminal geometry.

value.mitigation: three-sided slip 11 m inner width sized from the measured hull, plus a boat at BOTH ferry terminals so a drifted boat cannot strand the crossing

params.text: SEQ 34 IS A PHANTOM RECORD. It is mine, op zones_generate, role road_segment, and the command it describes WAS NEVER SENT. Produced by the LiveBuilder(dry=True) defect: dry mode still APPENDS its records and still runs check_expect against the LIVE server, so the record was written, nothing was sent, and the postcondition failed with zone_ctrl want 8 got 0 for zones [[-1,-1],[0,-1],[0,0],[1,0],[1,1],[2,0],[2,1],[3,1]]. NOT deleted and NOT rewritten: the chain is hash-linked and an append-only log with a labelled wart is worth more than an edited one. ON REPLAY IT IS BENIGN, and the reasoning is recorded rather than assumed: zones_generate is idempotent, and on a replay the zones really are generated, so the postcondition that failed at write time PASSES at replay time. It self-heals. That is luck specific to THIS op -- a phantom objects_clear or spawn_plan would NOT self-heal. Nobody uses dry=True again; the pre-flight is `ribbon.py --validate`, which builds the records, runs schema.validate, appends nothing and touches no console.

params.method: MEASURED: the same 6,113 written terrain samples of segment T3-temple-meadhall run through both clearance implementations. roads/poi.py::verdict_for_points returned CLEAR; settlements/clearance.py::verdict_for_samples (canonical, per-type max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM)) REFUSED with 5 violations.

value.general_form: Two checks answering the same question from different inputs will eventually disagree; the fix is a shared input, not a reconciliation.
value.note_the_distinction: T3 PASSES under the per-operation rule later ruled (destructive=False). That does NOT retract the finding: the original verdict was wrong for the wrong reason.
value.resolution: roads/poi.py::verdict_for_points DELETED; ribbon.py::location_check delegates to clearance.py; poi.py keeps only the routing raster (a per-cell forbid grid over an island is a different question from a verdict on a point set) and now reads max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) too, which is why the router and the gate cannot disagree.
value.why_it_matters: This was the segment I was about to build FIRST. Consolidating the instruments did not merely remove a duplicate, it caught a WRONG VERDICT on the first live write. The wrong verdict came from an INFERRED 11 m piece overshoot generalised from ONE observation, where the canonical instrument has znviewReachM MEASURED per type over all 177 types.

params.text: CLEAR-RADIUS POLICY IS PER OPERATION AND BOTH BEHAVIOURS ARE CORRECT, recorded so a future reader does not see two and conclude one is a bug. Crossings CLIPS its objects_clear radius (13.1 -> 10.3 m, poi_clipped true, binding instance named) because the clear exists only to make room for a deck it has already sized, and a smaller clear still admits the structure. SettleBuild REFUSES, because a clipped radius leaves forest standing against a wall and a town pad needs its whole footprint clear. RoadNet does NEITHER: this pipeline emits NO objects_clear at all, so it has no clearing radius to bound. A road ribbon DELETES NOTHING, which is exactly the claim that earns it the non-destructive clearance budget, and it is verifiable from my own records rather than asserted.

FORDS AND CAUSEWAYS ARE TERRAIN AND THEREFORE RoadNet's; BRIDGES ARE STRUCTURES AND THEREFORE Crossings'. Boundary agreed with Crossings and recorded once. The test is MEASURED and is DEPTH, not length: ground no more than 1.0 m below the water plane (y=30.0, ZoneSystem::c_WaterLevel, a static literal float32(30.)) can be filled to road freeboard well inside the measured +/-8 m ApplyToHeightmap clamp, so it is a levelled paved causeway at ANY length; anything deeper is a bridge. The first version of this test used an 8 m LENGTH cap and it produced a 450 m 'bridge' over a tidal flat on the dock approach and turned the entire 346 m west-isle link between the two bridge abutments into a bridge -- the mirror image of planning a 12 m bridge over a 40 m river.
